spec: MAdES — locating, parsing and rebuilding blocks (§a.1, §a.3, §a.5, §a.12, §a.13)
generatedFrom: the reference implementation, over the cases of reference/test/mades.test.mjs as of v1.10
note: Each case is a whole document and the expected reading of every block in it. The documents are small and mostly unsigned on purpose: each isolates one rule, and what these cases pin is where a block is, what it says and what it signs, not whether a key produced it. Until v1.10.1 they existed only as reference tests, where no second implementation could run them. The shape is described in vectors/README.md.
rules: The opening marker counts only at the start of a line, and never inside a fenced code block (§a.1).
Every line in a block is a comment, a blank or a well-formed field. From block version 4 anything else makes the block unsupported (§a.1, §a.5).
The signing input is the canonical content, a line feed, the comment lines in document order and the fields sorted by key, without signature and timestamp (§a.3).
Signature blocks and archive layers are one sequence. A layer covers the §a.2 canonicalisation of everything before its own opening marker (§a.13).

cases.name: an indented key after a list item is counted
cases.note: What a list of maps looks like. The syntax has lists of strings and maps of strings, nothing nested, so both indented keys are lines the reader cannot place. Before spec v1.5 the reference dropped them silently and gave a verdict over a block it had only partly read.

x

<!-- mades-sig
version: 5
covers:

cases.name: a version 3 block is read under version 3 rules
cases.note: Version 3 signed only the first comment line. The block version decides, not the reader, so signatures made then keep verifying. A verifier SHOULD also warn that the second line is outside the signature (§a.5).
cases.document:
content

<!-- mades-sig
# first
# second
version: 3
signer: a@b.example
-->

cases.name: covers: entries in the order written, inside the signing input
cases.note: Order is kept, never sorted. Each entry is digest, media type, and the rest of the line as the name, so a name may contain spaces. The list is in the signing input, so a changed digest is a changed signature.
